newsitem.title: BRAZIL: 11 babies die in Brazil from suspect serum - report.
newsitem.headline: 11 babies die in Brazil from suspect serum - report.

text.p: Eleven newborn babies and one adult have died in Brazil after being injected with serum that officials suspect may have been contaminated, newspapers reported on Saturday.

O Globo newspaper said nine babies and an adult had died in a hospital in Campinas, Sao Paulo state. On Friday, authorities at another hospital in nearby Limeira confirmed two babies there had also died, Globo said.
"The batch of contaminated serum was distributed to another 80 cities," the paper wrote.
Officials at the Santa Casa Misericordia hospital in Limeira declined to confirm the report and no one was available for comment at the Sao Paulo state health department.
Brazil's public health system has been beset by several tragedies in the past year.

Last October, poor hygiene standards killed 20 babies in a maternity ward in the northern state of Roraima, on Brazil's border with Venezuela. Nearly 100 elderly people were killed by bacterial infection in a Rio de Janeiro geriatric clinic between April and July.
Early this week, the government annouced new aims for health care, recognising that demand for medical treatment far outstripped supply.

Health Minister Carlos Alburquerque said more than 10 million Brazilians lacked access to basic health care and said the government would turn to private health insurers and the states and cities to make up the shortfall.
